# **1\. Introduction** {#1.-introduction}

## **1.1 Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the Pickleball Serve Classifier & Coaching App, Version 1.0, a standalone, on-device mobile application that processes side-view video from a single monocular smartphone camera to classify pickleball serve subtypes and generate expert-grounded corrective feedback. This document is intended for use by the development team, the faculty adviser, and the thesis review panel involved in the study “A Multimodal Computer Vision Framework for Pickleball Serve Subtype Classification and Rule-based Form Coaching.”

This SRS covers the requirements for the mobile-deployed serve evaluation pipeline described in Chapter 4 of the associated thesis. It does not cover the offline Python/TensorFlow model training environment, which is treated as a development tool rather than an end-user deliverable.

## **1.2 Document Conventions** {#1.2-document-conventions}

Each requirement in this document is uniquely identified using the format REQ-\<Section\>-\<Number\> (e.g., REQ-4.1-1). Requirements are prioritized as High, Medium, or Low based on their criticality to the study's research questions and evaluation metrics. Mandatory requirements use the word “shall”; optional or desired behavior uses “should” or “may.” Functional and non-functional requirement identifiers in Sections 4 and 5 of this SRS correspond directly to the FR and NFR numbering originally used in Section 4.5.1 of the thesis; that cross-reference is noted in brackets where applicable (e.g., \[FR4\], \[NFR2\]).

## **1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions** {#1.3-intended-audience-and-reading-suggestions}

This document is intended for the student researchers and developers (Ethan Job T. Leones and Joseph Gabriel Pascua), the faculty adviser (Glenn B. Pepito), and the thesis review panel.

●        Developers should read Sections 3–5 in full, as these define the interfaces, features, and measurable constraints that guide implementation.

●        The faculty adviser and panel may focus on Sections 1–2 for a high-level understanding of scope and objectives, and on Sections  4.3 and 5.1 for the measurable acceptance criteria (e.g., 85% classification accuracy, two-second latency) against which the system will be evaluated.

The document is organized to first present overall product context (Section 2), followed by external interface requirements (Section 3), detailed functional features (Section 4), and non-functional requirements (Section 5).

## **1.4 Product Scope** {#1.4-product-scope}

The Pickleball Serve Classifier & Coaching App is a standalone, on-device mobile The Pickleball Serve Classifier & Coaching App is a standalone, on-device mobile application that processes a side-view smartphone video of a player's serve through three independent computer vision streams: kinematic pose sequence, paddle orientation, and ball landing placement. These streams are fused at the decision level to classify the serve into one of three biomechanical subtypes (Drive, Lob, or Topspin) adapted from pickleball coaching literature (Prime Time Pickleball, 2023).

# **2\. Overall Description** {#2.-overall-description}

## **2.1 Product Perspective** {#2.1-product-perspective}

The Pickleball Serve Classifier & Coaching App is a new, standalone Android mobile application. It is not a replacement for an existing system and is not a component of a larger enterprise system, nor does it interface with any external system, cloud backend, or third-party API. Per the architectural style defined in the thesis, all functional processes, camera capture, computer vision feature extraction, TensorFlow Lite inference, rule-based fusion logic, and feedback rendering, execute entirely within a single React Native application process on the user's smartphone.

## **2.2 Product Functions** {#2.2-product-functions}

At a high level, the system performs the following major functions:

* Automatically detects the presence of a player and paddle in the camera frame and initiates serve recording.

* Automatically detects ball-bounce contact and terminates recording to begin processing.

* Extracts a 33-joint skeletal pose sequence via BlazePose and passes it through a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) sequence model to produce a Serve Type classification label. 

* Detects the paddle via YOLOv26s and computes its orientation angle via OpenCV's minAreaRect, producing a Directional Deviation State.

* Detects ball landing coordinates via YOLOv26s and maps them to a real-world court placement zone via planar homography, producing a Spatial Placement Zone.

* Fuses the three independent stream outputs exclusively at the decision level.

* Queries a human-encoded, expert-validated IF-THEN rule engine to generate corrective or encouraging feedback text.

* Displays final serve type, directional deviation state, spatial placement, and feedback to the player, gracefully degrading to an “insufficient data” notice for any stream that fails.

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics** {#2.3-user-classes-and-characteristics}

| User Class | Characteristics | Privileges/Access |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Player (End User) | Non-technical, recreational-to-intermediate pickleball player; interacts with the system solely by mounting the phone on a tripod and serving; requires no account creation, login, or configuration. | Standard, single-role access (the sole system actor), per the Use Case Diagram in Appendix B. |

## *Note.* Coaches, academies, and researchers are described elsewhere in the thesis as beneficiaries and stakeholders of the study, but are not modeled as direct system actors in the current single-user, on-device design.

## **2.4 Operating Environment** {#2.4-operating-environment}

The production application runs on Android smartphones, using a React Native runtime with an embedded TensorFlow Lite inference engine. Hardware validation is scoped to two mid-range Android devices:

●        Xiaomi Redmi Note 12 (6GB RAM, Android 14): the primary lower-bound inference baseline.

●        CMF Phone 2 Pro (8GB RAM, Android 16): the escalation target should the Redmi Note 12 fail to meet the two-second latency threshold.

The application requires no network connectivity at runtime. Input video must be captured at 1920x1080 resolution and 60 frames per second with the camera mounted 2 meters above ground, angled downward toward the net, on the player’s dominant-hand side of the court.

Model development, training, and evaluation occur in an offline Python/TensorFlow environment and are outside the scope of this SRS; only the resulting converted TFLite model artifact is part of the deployed application. 

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints** {#2.5-design-and-implementation-constraints}

* The system shall be implemented as a standalone, fully offline mobile application with a React Native front end and an embedded TensorFlow Lite inference engine, with no cloud backend, no RESTful or event-driven integration, and no external database. 

* Only open-source, freely available tools may be used (Python, TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, MediaPipe/BlazePose, YOLOv26s, OpenCV, React Native, GitHub, Visual Studio Code, Google Forms). No licensed or commercially paid software is permitted.

* Inference must meet a two-second end-to-end latency target on the Xiaomi Redmi Note 12 lower-bound hardware.

* The system is delimited to a single outdoor recreational court under artificial night lighting (8:00–10:00 PM), a fixed camera position and angle, and a single monocular camera. No 3D reconstruction or multi-camera hardware is used. 

* Classification is constrained to three pickleball-native biomechanical serve subtypes (Drive, Lob, Topspin); if these are determined to be indistinguishable in pickleball, the system must fall back to the binary legal-serve taxonomy (volley serve, drop serve) defined by USA Pickleball (2026). 

* All corrective feedback logic must be human-encoded IF-THEN rules derived from GPF-endorsed coach commentary and independently validated by a third GPF-endorsed coach before deployment. Feedback text may not be machine-generated.

* The system is delimited to right-handed players only; the trained GRU model and encoded rule base reflect right-handed serve mechanics exclusively, and left-handed serve input will produce incorrect outputs rather than merely unreliable ones. 

  ## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies** {#2.6-assumptions-and-dependencies}

* Assumes the end user positions the smartphone per the fixed camera specification (height, angle, side) defined in Section 2.4; results are not guaranteed to be reliable if this setup is not followed.

* Assumes court boundary lines are visible and undistorted in-frame to allow homographic calibration.

* Depends on the continued availability and API stability of the open-source frameworks used (MediaPipe/BlazePose, YOLOv26s, OpenCV, TensorFlow Lite).

* Depends on the trained GRU classifier meeting the 85% stratified cross-validation accuracy threshold (REQ-4.3-3 / NFR2) before the feedback engine is considered reliable for deployment.

* Assumes continued availability of the three GPF-endorsed coaches (Coach A for good-form baselines, Coach B for annotation, Coach C for independent validation) throughout data collection and validation.

* Assumes the end user configures the smartphone camera to a minimum of 60 frames per second prior to recording.

* Assumes the end user's smartphone camera applies automatic exposure control sufficient to prevent motion blur under artificial court lighting (8:00–10:00 PM); shutter speed cannot be directly set or verified by the application on mid-range Android devices, and inadequate exposure settings represent a known environmental vulnerability documented in Section 4.1 of the thesis.

  # **3\. External Interface Requirements** {#3.-external-interface-requirements}

  ## **3.1 User Interfaces** {#3.1-user-interfaces}

  The application uses a single-screen layout consisting of a live camera feed across the top (with a camera-index dropdown for input selection and a status indicator reflecting pipeline state), and four result cards spanning the bottom of the screen: Serve Type, Paddle Angle, Ball Landing, and Feedback.

  The system requires no manual “record” control: recording auto-initiates when a player and paddle are simultaneously detected (REQ-4.1-2) and auto-terminates one second after ball-bounce detection (REQ-4.1-3). While results are being calculated, all four cards display a shimmer placeholder (Figure 1).

  **Figure 1**

  *Wireframe (Detecting/Calculating state).* 

**![][image1]**

*Note.* The status indicator and shimmer placeholders on all four result cards reflect the active processing state. 

Once processing completes, cards populate with their respective outputs: a serve-type label with a good/bad-form tag and an inline reference to serve definitions; a numeric paddle angle with a directional tag (e.g., “Optimal,” “Too closed”); a half-court diagram marking the ball's landing zone; and the corrective or encouraging feedback string (Figure 2).

**Figure 2**

*Wireframe (Results Visible state).*

**![][image2]**  
If any upstream stream fails to produce a valid output, only the affected result card is replaced with an explicit “insufficient data” warning while the remaining cards populate normally, consistent with the partial-delivery requirement (REQ-4.5-1).

**Figure 3**

Wireframe (Insufficient Data state)

**![][image3]**

*Note.* The affected result card displays an explicit failure notice while all remaining cards populate normally.

## **3.4 Communications Interfaces** {#3.4-communications-interfaces}

None. Consistent with the standalone, offline architecture defined in the thesis, the system makes no network calls and has no email/SMTP, HTTPS, or messaging integration. No data is transmitted off the device at runtime.

# **4\. System Features** {#4.-system-features}

This section describes the major features of the deployed application. Each feature is organized by its position in the processing pipeline, from serve capture through feedback delivery.

## 

## **4.1 Auto Serve Detection & Capture** {#4.1-auto-serve-detection-&-capture}

### ***4.1.1 Description and Priority*** {#4.1.1-description-and-priority}

Automatically starts serve recording once the user is detected and stops serve recording without requiring manual input from the player. 

Priority: High.

### ***4.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences*** {#4.1.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

●Player enters the camera frame with a paddle simultaneously visible → system detects the concurrent presence of a player and paddle in the live feed → the system auto-initiates recording of the serve sequence. 

●Player strikes the ball and it lands on the court → system detects the ball-bounce contact event in the video stream → system auto-terminates recording exactly 1 second after the bounce and begins processing.

### ***4.1.3 Functional Requirements*** {#4.1.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-4.1-1 | The system shall ingest a live side-view video stream matching the recording specifications defined in Section 2.4. \[FR1\] | High |
| REQ-4.1-2 | The system shall auto-initiate the computer vision pipeline when it detects a player and paddle simultaneously present in the camera feed. \[FR2\]  | High |
| REQ-4.1-3 | The system shall auto-terminate the recording and begin processing exactly 1 second after a ball bounce is detected in the video stream. \[FR3\] | High |

## 

## **4.2 Multimodal Feature Extraction** {#4.2-multimodal-feature-extraction}

### ***4.2.1 Description and Priority*** {#4.2.1-description-and-priority}

Processes each captured serve simultaneously across three independent computer vision streams (kinematic, equipment, spatial).

Priority: High.

### ***4.2.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences*** {#4.2.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* A raw serve clip is captured → the kinematic stream extracts a 33-joint skeletal tensor via BlazePose → the equipment stream extracts a continuous paddle-angle scalar via YOLOv26s and OpenCV's minAreaRect → the spatial stream extracts ball pixel coordinates via YOLOv26s object tracking → each stream produces its intermediate output independently before advancing to fusion.   
* The equipment stream computes a raw minAreaRect angle bounded within a 90-degree range → the aspect ratio of the detected bounding rectangle is evaluated to determine whether the paddle's long axis is oriented vertically or horizontally → the angle is corrected accordingly to resolve the inherent 90-degree axis ambiguity before the Directional Deviation State is produced.   
* Fusion produces a valid combined state, but no rule in the IF-THEN rule base matches the specific combination of serve type, directional deviation, and placement zone → the system returns a predefined fallback notification to the user rather than an empty or undefined output, consistent with REQ-4.4-4. 


  ### ***4.2.3 Functional Requirements*** {#4.2.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-4.2-1 | The system shall process each captured serve simultaneously across three independent computer vision streams: a GRU operating on skeletal pose keypoint sequences extracted by BlazePose, a YOLOv26s detection pipeline supplying paddle orientation via OpenCV's minAreaRect, and a YOLOv26s ball detection pipeline supplying landing coordinates for homographic projection. No signal from one stream shall influence another prior to the decision-level fusion stage. \[FR4\]  | High |
| REQ-4.2-2 | The equipment stream shall resolve minAreaRect's inherent 90-degree axis ambiguity using the aspect ratio of the detected bounding rectangle to determine whether the long axis is oriented vertically or horizontally, correcting the angle accordingly before producing the Directional Deviation State. \[FR4\]  | Medium |
| REQ-4.2-3 | The spatial stream shall project detected ball-landing pixel coordinates into real-world 2D court coordinates using a homography matrix computed from visible court boundary line intersections. \[FR4\]  | High |

## 

## 

## **4.3 Decision-Level Fusion & Classification** {#4.3-decision-level-fusion-&-classification}

### ***4.3.1 Description and Priority*** {#4.3.1-description-and-priority}

Combines the three independent stream outputs only at the final decision stage to produce a unified serve classification. 

Priority: High.

### ***4.3.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences*** {#4.3.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* The three streams each complete processing and produce a Serve Type, Directional Deviation State, and Placement Zone → the system evaluates the GRU's softmax confidence against the 0.60 threshold → if confidence is sufficient, the system evaluates the three states jointly against the rule base; if insufficient, the system withholds classification-dependent feedback and returns a low-confidence notification.

  ### ***4.3.3 Functional Requirements*** {#4.3.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-4.3-1 | The system shall fuse the independent outputs of the three streams exclusively at the decision level to produce a biomechanical serve subtype classification (Drive, Lob, or Topspin) alongside a paddle orientation angle and a spatial placement zone for ball landing. \[FR5\]  | High |
| REQ-4.3-2 | At inference time, the system shall apply a softmax confidence threshold of 0.60, withholding all feedback and returning a low-confidence notification to the user when the GRU's maximum class probability falls below this value. \[NFR3\]  | High |
| REQ-4.3-3 | The GRU classifier shall achieve a minimum stratified cross-validation accuracy of 85% across all three serve subtypes before the feedback engine is considered sufficiently reliable for deployment. \[NFR2\]  | High |

  ## *Note:* REQ-4.3-2 and REQ-4.3-3 are classified as nonfunctional requirements in the thesis (NFR3 and NFR2 respectively) but are grouped here because they directly gate the classification feature's operational behavior and cannot be meaningfully evaluated independently of it. 

## 

  ## **4.4 Rule-Based Corrective Feedback Generation** {#4.4-rule-based-corrective-feedback-generation}

  ### ***4.4.1 Description and Priority*** {#4.4.1-description-and-priority}

  Converts the fused classification state into a specific, expert-grounded corrective or encouraging feedback string for the player, without relying on generative machine learning. Priority: High.

  ### ***4.4.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences*** {#4.4.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* Fusion produces a valid combined state (serve type \+ directional deviation \+ placement) → system queries the human-encoded IF-THEN rule base → a matching rule fires and returns its corresponding feedback string → if all intermediate states fall within acceptable parameters, a positive-confirmation rule fires instead, returning an encouragement string.  
* The GRU confidence falls below the 0.60 threshold defined in REQ-4.3-2 → fusion is halted and the rule engine is not queried → the system returns a low-confidence notification in place of corrective feedback, consistent with the selective classification behavior specified in Section 4.3. 

  ### ***4.4.3 Functional Requirements*** {#4.4.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-4.4-1 | Following fusion, the system shall query the human-encoded IF-THEN rule engine to generate corrective feedback strings corresponding to the fused classification output. \[FR6\]  | High |
| REQ-4.4-2 | All corrective feedback strings delivered by the rule engine shall originate from rules grounded in Coach B's deviation commentary and independently validated by Coach C through blind review prior to deployment.  | High |
| REQ-4.4-3 | If all intermediate states (serve type, directional deviation, placement) fall within acceptable parameters, the system shall fire a positive confirmation rule and return an encouragement string rather than a corrective one.  | Medium |
| REQ-4.4-4 | If no rule in the IF-THEN rule base matches the fused state, the system shall return a predefined fallback notification to the user rather than producing undefined behavior or an empty output.  | Medium |

## 

  ## **4.5 Graceful Degradation on Stream Failure** {#4.5-graceful-degradation-on-stream-failure}

  ### ***4.5.1 Description and Priority*** {#4.5.1-description-and-priority}

  Ensures the player still receives usable results when one of the three computer vision streams fails to produce a valid output. 

  Priority: Medium.

  ### ***4.5.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences*** {#4.5.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* One stream (e.g., the spatial stream) fails to detect its target (e.g., the ball is occluded) → the system delivers the outputs of the remaining valid streams normally → the affected result card is replaced with an explicit “insufficient data” notification (e.g., “Ball not detected. Ensure the ball is visible throughout the serve.”) while all other cards populate as usual.

  ### ***4.5.3 Functional Requirements*** {#4.5.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-4.5-1 | Where one or more signals are unavailable due to detection failure, the system shall deliver results derived from whichever streams produced valid output and explicitly notify the user of which signal was absent, consistent with the independent stream architecture that late fusion enables (Yang & Gulbahar, 2025). \[FR7\] | Medium |

  # **5\. Other Nonfunctional Requirements** {#5.-other-nonfunctional-requirements}

  ## **5.1 Performance Requirements** {#5.1-performance-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-5.1-1 | The system shall deliver its complete classification output and corrective feedback within two seconds of serve completion. \[NFR1\] | High |
| REQ-5.1-2 | The deployed TFLite model shall perform within the two-second latency target on the lower-bound hardware baseline, the Xiaomi Redmi Note 12\. If this target is exceeded, testing shall escalate to the CMF Phone 2 Pro to determine whether the hardware requirement itself, rather than the model architecture, requires revision. \[NFR4\]  | High |
| REQ-5.1-3 | Input video shall be captured at a minimum of 1920x1080 resolution and 60 frames per second to support downstream feature extraction fidelity. | High |
| REQ-5.1-4 | Because TFLite's GPU delegate does not support quantized models on Android, quantized GRU inference shall execute on CPU; the two-second latency target in REQ-5.1-1 must be validated specifically under CPU inference conditions on the Xiaomi Redmi Note 12\.  | High |

  ## **5.2 Safety Requirements** {#5.2-safety-requirements}

  The system is advisory in nature, non-safety-critical, and does not control any physical hardware; it produces corrective coaching feedback only and does not intervene in a player's physical actions. No safety requirements beyond standard graceful handling of detection failure (REQ-4.5-1) have been identified.

  ## 

  ## **5.3 Security Requirements** {#5.3-security-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-5.3-1 | The system shall require no user accounts, login portals, or authentication, as it operates entirely on-device with no personal data transmitted to external servers. | High |
| REQ-5.3-2 | End-user video clips shall be processed locally and discarded after the inference and feedback generation cycle is complete; no runtime video data shall be retained on the device beyond the processing cycle. | High |

  Standard web-application vulnerability classes, including those listed in the OWASP Top 10 such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and authentication bypass, are outside the scope of this system's security requirements. Because the deployed application performs no network communication, maintains no remote or local database, and requires no user authentication, the architectural conditions that make these vulnerabilities possible are absent by design. This scoping does not represent an oversight but a direct consequence of the standalone, offline architecture established in Section 2.5. 


  The runtime auto-deletion policy in REQ-5.3-2 applies only to the deployed application. The 690-clip research dataset used during model construction and validation is retained separately under documented informed consent for training purposes, and is outside the scope of the deployed system's security requirements.

  ## 

  ## **5.4 Software Quality Attributes** {#5.4-software-quality-attributes}

| Attribute | Description | Governing Requirements |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Reliability | The GRU classifier must meet an 85% minimum stratified cross-validation accuracy across all three serve subtypes before deployment. The system must abstain from delivering feedback when classification confidence falls below 0.60 rather than act on uncertain predictions. The system must additionally produce defined behavior under all possible fused state combinations, returning a predefined fallback notification when no rule match is found rather than failing silently.  | REQ-4.3-2, REQ-4.3-3, REQ-4.4-4 |
| Usability | The player-facing interface requires no manual controls. Recording starts and stops automatically based on player-paddle detection and ball-bounce detection respectively. All four result outputs are presented on a single screen without requiring navigation.  | REQ-4.1-2, REQ-4.1-3  |
| Maintainability | The mobile front end follows a strict Component-Based Development paradigm with modular, reusable components covering camera capture, feedback display, and results rendering. The ML pipeline uses procedural Python scripting appropriate to its sequential data-transformation nature. Both are version-controlled via a feature-branch GitHub workflow.  | Section 2.5, Section 4.7.2 of the thesis  |
|  Portability |  The deployed application targets Android smartphones only, validated specifically on the Xiaomi Redmi Note 12 (6GB RAM, Android 14\) as the lower-bound baseline and the CMF Phone 2 Pro (8GB RAM, Android 16\) as the escalation target. Performance on devices below these specifications is untested and not guaranteed. The system is additionally not portable to left-handed players, as the trained GRU model and encoded rule base reflect right-handed serve mechanics exclusively.  |  REQ-5.1-2, Constraint 6 (Section 2.5)  |
|  Availability | Because the system requires no network connectivity, availability is bounded only by on-device resource availability such as battery and memory, with no dependency on external service uptime.  |  Section 2.5, REQ-5.3-1  |
| Traceability | Every IF-THEN rule in the feedback rule base must be traceable to a specific deviation comment provided by Coach B during annotation and must carry an independent validation record from Coach C's blind review prior to deployment. No corrective feedback string enters the deployed system without a documented expert derivation and validation chain.  | REQ-4.4-2 |

  ## 

  ## **5.5 Business Rules** {#5.5-business-rules}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQ-5.5-1 | Only right-handed players are supported by the current classification model and rule base; the training dataset and camera positioning are specific to right-handed serve mechanics. | High |
| REQ-5.5-2 | If Coach B determines that the Drive, Lob, and Topspin taxonomy cannot be consistently and reliably identified in pickleball, the classification protocol will fall back to the binary legal serve definitions (volley serve and drop serve) established by USA Pickleball (2026), and the inability to transfer the instructional taxonomy shall be documented as a formal limitation.  | Medium |
| REQ-5.5-3 | No corrective feedback string may be deployed to the rule base unless it has passed independent blind validation by a third GPF-endorsed coach (Coach C). | High |
| REQ-5.5-4 | The system shall not classify or provide feedback on any stroke type other than the serve (e.g., dinks, drives, and volleys are out of scope), and shall not function as a rules-compliance engine for USA Pickleball serve legality.  | High |

# 

  # **6\. Other Requirements** {#6.-other-requirements}

  **6.1 Data Collection and Research Ethics**

  Documented informed consent shall be obtained from all video recording subjects  (Coach A and Beginner Players 1 through 4\) prior to any video recording session. Separate documented consent shall be obtained from Coach B and Coach C covering their respective annotation and blind validation activities, as neither coach is recorded on video. This requirement governs the research and data-collection phase and is distinct from the runtime privacy behavior of the deployed application specified in Section 5.3. 


  All research-phase data handling, including individual clip file management, YouTube playlist organization, backup protocol, and bulk integrity review, shall follow the data collection protocol defined in Section 4.3.1 of the associated thesis document. 


  

  **6.2 Licensing**

  The licensing status of the trained GRU model weights and other original research artifacts produced by this study is subject to the intellectual property policy of the University of San Carlos and will be determined upon thesis completion. All third-party tools and frameworks used in development are open-source or freely available, as specified in Section 2.5, and are used in accordance with their respective licenses.

# **Appendix A: Glossary** {#appendix-a:-glossary}

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| BlazePose | A two-stage, 33-keypoint human pose estimation model optimized for on-device mobile inference within the MediaPipe framework. |
| Directional Deviation State | The intermediate output of the equipment stream, representing not merely whether the paddle angle falls outside acceptable thresholds but specifically the direction of the violation (e.g., Optimal, Too Closed, Too Open). This is an original term defined by this study.  |
| GPF-endorsed coach | A pickleball coach holding active certification from a recognized coaching body (e.g., PPR, PGA, PCI, IFPA, or RPO), used in this study as the standard for expert domain-knowledge sources. |
| GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) | A recurrent neural network variant that models temporal sequences using reset and update gates; used here to classify serve type from pose keypoint sequences over time. |
| Homography | A projective transformation, represented as a 3×3 matrix, that maps 2D image pixel coordinates onto a real-world planar reference surface (the court). |
| HPE (Human Pose Estimation) | A computer vision task that detects and tracks anatomical keypoints (joints, extremities) to form a skeletal representation of body configuration. |
| Late Fusion | A multimodal integration strategy in which each data stream is processed independently through its own feature extractor and combined only at the final decision stage. |
| MediaPipe | A cross-platform framework providing the deployment infrastructure (graph-based calculators, streaming, GPU acceleration) that runs models like BlazePose on-device. |
| minAreaRect | An OpenCV computational geometry function that computes the minimum-area rotated bounding rectangle of a detected object contour; used to extract the paddle's orientation angle. |
| minAreaRect 90-degree axis ambiguity | A geometric limitation of OpenCV's minAreaRect function in which the returned angle is inherently bounded within a 90-degree range due to the symmetric nature of rectangular contours, making it impossible to distinguish whether the paddle's long axis is oriented vertically or horizontally from the raw angle value alone. This ambiguity is resolved using the aspect ratio of the detected bounding rectangle.  |
| Softmax Confidence Threshold | A selective classification mechanism in which the GRU model's output probability distribution is evaluated before feedback is delivered. When the highest class probability falls below the defined threshold of 0.60, the system withholds all feedback and returns a low-confidence notification to the user rather than acting on an uncertain prediction, consistent with REQ-4.3-2.  |
| TFLite (TensorFlow Lite) | A lightweight inference framework that converts trained TensorFlow models into a compact format for on-device execution on mobile and embedded hardware. |
| YOLOv26s | The small-scale variant of the YOLO26 real-time object detection architecture; used here to detect the paddle and ball within each video frame. |
